project.name: in-progress
project.description: Local-first browser control plane for durable coding-agent terminals and project-bound views.

decisions.title: Plugin authority
decisions.question: How should external project views receive host data and authority?
decisions.rationale: A view needs useful project context without inheriting cookies, DOM access, arbitrary network access, or a general host execution surface.

alternatives.label: Opaque capability frames
alternatives.description: Run static views in opaque-origin iframes and broker explicit project-bound methods over a MessagePort.
alternatives.impact: Strong browser isolation and auditable least authority, with a small versioned protocol.

brief.objective: Preserve opaque-origin static plugins with manifest-declared, project-bound MessagePort capabilities.
constraints: Keep host cookies, DOM, storage, external network access, and generic process execution unavailable.
Require host-owned enforcement for every capability and privileged user confirmation.
acceptance: A plugin can invoke only methods declared by its validated manifest for the selected host project.
Navigation or frame disposal permanently closes the channel, and direct host API access remains impossible.

alternatives.label: Trusted same-origin modules
alternatives.description: Load every installed view as a host-origin module with direct application APIs.
alternatives.impact: Simpler composition, but any plugin compromise becomes a full host and shell compromise.

brief.objective: Replace iframe plugins with reviewed same-origin modules and a typed host extension API.
constraints: Make installation explicitly equivalent to trusting host code.
Preserve project scoping and navigation lifecycle semantics.
acceptance: The extension API is typed, versioned, and rejects incompatible modules at startup.
Documentation and UI disclose that plugin code has host-page authority.

alternatives.label: Per-plugin daemons
alternatives.description: Run each plugin behind a separate OS process and narrow authenticated protocol.
alternatives.impact: A stronger process boundary with materially greater packaging, supervision, and policy complexity.

brief.objective: Move plugin execution into separately supervised least-privilege services.
constraints: Assign explicit filesystem, network, CPU, memory, and lifetime limits per service.
Retain the browser's opaque-origin presentation boundary.
acceptance: Compromising one plugin service grants neither another plugin's data nor terminal authority.
Service authentication, restart, upgrade, and protocol compatibility have deterministic tests.

decisions.title: Terminal lifecycle
decisions.question: Which component should own durable coding-agent shell sessions?
decisions.rationale: The browser must detach and reconnect without interrupting work, while terminal input ownership, replay, and backpressure remain bounded.

alternatives.label: Host-owned Bun PTY
alternatives.description: Keep each PTY in the long-lived Bun process and reconnect browsers through one-use tickets.
alternatives.impact: Tight protocol control and minimal dependencies; sessions end when the host process ends.

brief.objective: Retain host-owned Bun PTYs with bounded replay, writer leases, backpressure, and session-bound WebSocket tickets.
constraints: Keep terminal bytes out of durable storage.
Reject cross-origin upgrades and bound every input, output, replay, and queued buffer.
acceptance: Browser disconnect and reconnect preserve a live process and bounded recent output.
A one-use ticket can attach only to its browser session, project, and PTY.

alternatives.label: tmux-backed sessions
alternatives.description: Delegate process persistence and replay to tmux, attaching the web terminal to named sessions.
alternatives.impact: Survives host restarts, but adds an external control plane and terminal-state translation.

brief.objective: Use project-scoped tmux sessions as the canonical durable process owner.
constraints: Authenticate and validate every tmux target name.
Preserve single-writer browser leases and bounded web delivery.
acceptance: A host restart reconnects to existing project sessions without duplicate processes.
Untrusted project strings cannot select or create a session outside their assigned namespace.

alternatives.label: User-service sessions
alternatives.description: Launch each agent under a transient systemd user service with a separate PTY relay.
alternatives.impact: Explicit lifetime and resource controls, with significant relay and recovery machinery.

brief.objective: Move process ownership into transient systemd user units with inspectable resource policy.
constraints: Keep the PTY relay authenticated and project-bound.
Define deterministic cleanup for exited, failed, and abandoned units.
acceptance: Sessions survive host restarts and expose bounded CPU, memory, and lifetime policy.
Every unit and relay is reconciled after interrupted startup or shutdown.

decisions.title: Remote boundary
decisions.question: How should owner devices reach the workstation control plane?
decisions.rationale: Remote terminal input equals the workstation user's shell authority, so reachability and identity must stay narrow and explicit.

alternatives.label: Loopback plus Tailscale Serve
alternatives.description: Bind only to loopback and use private Tailscale HTTPS plus owner identity headers.
alternatives.impact: Phone access with a small application perimeter, dependent on tailnet policy and device security.

brief.objective: Preserve loopback-only HTTP behind private Tailscale Serve HTTPS.
constraints: Reject non-loopback binding by default and require exact allowed owner identities.
Never treat forwarded identity headers as trustworthy on a directly reachable backend.
acceptance: Direct LAN/public peers cannot reach the service under supported configuration.
Proxy requests require HTTPS, forwarding evidence, and the same identity throughout the browser session.

alternatives.label: Local browser only
alternatives.description: Remove remote access support and accept requests only from the workstation browser.
alternatives.impact: Smallest network perimeter, but no phone or off-workstation workflow.

brief.objective: Constrain the product to direct loopback browsers and remove proxy identity handling.
constraints: Keep same-origin CSRF and WebSocket origin enforcement.
Remove remote-specific configuration and documentation.
acceptance: Every accepted request resolves to a direct loopback authority without forwarding headers.
The UI and installation flow make remote access unsupported rather than merely undocumented.

alternatives.label: Mutual-TLS gateway
alternatives.description: Expose a private-network HTTPS gateway that authenticates owner-device client certificates.
alternatives.impact: Independent device identity with certificate issuance, rotation, revocation, and proxy hardening costs.

brief.objective: Replace Tailscale identity with a loopback backend behind an mTLS-authenticated private gateway.
constraints: Pin the gateway-to-backend trust path and strip all caller-supplied identity headers.
Provide certificate rotation and immediate device revocation.
acceptance: Requests without an allowed unexpired client certificate never reach the application.
Application sessions bind to a stable certificate identity and reject identity changes.

decisions.title: Native integration boundary
decisions.question: How should plugins reach analyzers and tools that need filesystem or process authority?
decisions.rationale: Manifest data capabilities alone cannot safely express native execution, while a generic backend would turn plugin input into workstation command authority.

alternatives.label: Host-owned named adapters
alternatives.description: Configure trusted native code separately and expose only fixed, typed operations.
alternatives.impact: Narrow auditable authority with one maintained adapter per integration.

brief.objective: Retain host-configured Align, Drift, and Tree Complete adapters with fixed executables, roots, modes, and schemas.
constraints: Never accept executable, root, raw command, model, or runner mode from plugin RPC.
Bound process groups, deadlines, output, JSON shape, and returned host paths.
acceptance: Every native operation maps one manifest capability to one fixed host implementation.
Malformed input, incompatible output, path escape, timeout, or unconfigured authority fails closed.

alternatives.label: Generic plugin backend
alternatives.description: Let each plugin register an arbitrary host command and RPC surface in its manifest.
alternatives.impact: Fast extension development, but manifest installation becomes unconstrained same-user code execution.

brief.objective: Define a generic executable-backed plugin protocol with explicit installation-time trust.
constraints: Treat every backend plugin as full workstation-user code authority.
Separate backend lifecycle, logs, upgrades, and failure isolation from the browser host.
acceptance: Installation and UI clearly distinguish data-only plugins from full-authority backend plugins.
Backend crashes and malformed protocol messages cannot crash the control-plane process.

alternatives.label: Independent tool services
alternatives.description: Require native tools to expose separately managed authenticated loopback services.
alternatives.impact: Clear ownership boundaries and independent upgrades, with more daemons and credentials.

brief.objective: Move every native integration behind an independently supervised local service protocol.
constraints: Authenticate each host-to-service connection and pin project authority server-side.
Keep plugin code unable to connect to those services directly.
acceptance: A service receives only the project and operation authority assigned by host configuration.
Connection loss, version mismatch, and service compromise have explicit bounded failure behavior.
